sections.title: Habit and foliage
sections.text: Garden rue is a perennial subshrub, woody at the base, native to southern Europe and grown in gardens. It reaches about 70–100 cm. Its blue-green, alternate leaves are divided several times and have a strong scent.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Small greenish-yellow flowers with four or five petals are borne in corymbs. The fruit is a lobed capsule containing black seeds. The plate shows the divided foliage, yellow flowers and characteristic capsules.

sections.title: Toxicity and contact
sections.text: Rue contains phototoxic compounds. Sap or leaves can cause a skin reaction, with redness and sometimes blisters, when contact is followed by UV exposure. Large amounts are toxic if swallowed; no food use is recommended here.
